title: Myhill–Nerode as Admissible Forgetting
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in automata/formal languages, centered on the claim that state distinctions may be forgotten exactly when no admissible future observation distinguishes them. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that minimal DFA is the coarsest observational quotient preserving language behavior. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: standard theorem statement, worked DFA minimization, and quotient comparison, plus 1 additional evidence item.

title: Abstract Interpretation and CEGAR as Distinction Forgetting and Repair
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in formal methods/verification, centered on the claim that abstraction forgets distinctions; spurious counterexamples witness harmful forgetting; refinement restores required distinctions. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that CEGAR is a structured forget-execute-witness-repair loop. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: abstract interpretation prior art, finite abstraction example, and spurious counterexample, plus 1 additional evidence item.

title: MapReduce as Boundary Formation, Equivalence, and Closure
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in distributed data processing, centered on the claim that shuffle defines intermediate equivalence classes; reduce closes each class; combiners require composable local closure. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that key design determines which distinctions are preserved or forgotten; skew is boundary-load imbalance. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: canonical MapReduce model, word-count positive example, and non-associative/unsafe combiner counterexample, plus 2 additional evidence items.

title: Dynamic Programming as Sufficient State Retention
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in algorithms/optimization, centered on the claim that history may be forgotten only when the retained state preserves every distinction relevant to future optimal continuation. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that DP state design is a sufficiency problem; invalid states forget future-relevant information. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: Bellman principle, valid memoization state, and invalid state counterexample, plus 1 additional evidence item.

title: Dijkstra’s Algorithm as a Moving Closure Frontier
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in graph algorithms, centered on the claim that settled vertices cross an epistemic boundary when no remaining admissible path can improve their distance. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that nonnegative weights are the condition making finalization monotone and lawful. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: standard proof invariant, frontier trace, and negative-edge counterexample.

title: Relational Normalization and Lossless Join as Admissible Forgetting
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in database theory, centered on the claim that decomposition forgets structure only when dependencies permit exact reconstruction without spurious tuples. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that lossless decomposition is admissible reduction under a reconstruction obligation. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: functional dependencies, lossless decomposition, and lossy decomposition counterexample, plus 1 additional evidence item.

title: A* as Admissible Possibility Pruning
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in search/AI, centered on the claim that heuristics bound unexplored possibility without excluding a potentially optimal path. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that admissibility and consistency are distinct obligations on pruning and frontier closure. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: admissible heuristic example, inconsistent heuristic example, and frontier comparison.

title: Union–Find as Quotient Formation with Representation-Preserving Compression
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in data structures/algorithms, centered on the claim that union creates equivalence classes while path compression changes internal representation without changing observed class identity. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that quotient semantics separates abstract identity from implementation representation. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: small disjoint-set trace, path compression before/after, and equivalence invariant.

title: Garbage Collection as Safe Forgetting beyond Reachability
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in runtime systems, centered on the claim that objects outside the root-reachable observation boundary may be forgotten without changing admissible future execution. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that reclamation correctness is distinction irrelevance under reachability. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: mark-sweep trace, reachable/unreachable graph, and weak-reference caveat.

title: Max-Flow / Min-Cut as Boundary Capacity
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in graph algorithms/optimization, centered on the claim that flow is admissible transport through capacity-bounded interfaces and the min cut is the globally limiting boundary. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that capacity is a literal boundary constraint and cut certificates expose the limiting interface. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: small network, augmenting paths, and cut certificate.

title: Compiler Pipelines as Representation-Preserving Transport
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in compiler theory/programming languages, centered on the claim that each IR is a representation; passes are transports that must preserve declared semantics while possibly forgetting irrelevant distinctions. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that compiler correctness and optimization legality become explicit transport obligations. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: toy source-to-IR pipeline, semantics-preserving optimization, and miscompilation counterexample.

title: Bisimulation as Dynamic Admissible Identification
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in concurrency/transition systems, centered on the claim that states may share an observational identity when admissible transitions can be mutually matched. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that dynamic state quotienting requires transition-preserving rather than merely static observational equivalence. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: finite LTS, bisimilar pair, and trace-equivalent but non-bisimilar example.

title: Partial-Order Reduction as Safe Forgetting of Ordering Distinctions
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in concurrency/model checking, centered on the claim that ordering distinctions may be forgotten when independent actions commute relative to relevant observations. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that POR is admissible quotienting of execution traces under independence. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: two commuting actions, dependent action counterexample, and state-space reduction count.

title: Noninterference as an Information-Transport Boundary Condition
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in security/information flow, centered on the claim that changes behind a protected boundary must not induce unauthorized observable distinctions across it. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that information-flow security is a constrained transport/non-observability obligation. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: two-level system, noninterference witness, and declassification caveat.

title: Bloom Filters as Controlled One-Sided Distinction Loss
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in probabilistic data structures, centered on the claim that many concrete membership states intentionally collapse into one representation under an asymmetric error contract. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that false positives are budgeted quotient defects while false negatives are excluded by design. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: small bloom filter, collision witness, and false-positive rate discussion.
